🪔 Some nights at Pashupatinath are lit for the living. This one is lit for those we have lost.

Bala Chaturdashi falls on Monday, 7 December this year. Families keep an overnight vigil at Pashupatinath, lighting oil lamps in memory of loved ones who have passed away — then walk through the Shleshmantak forest beside the temple, scattering satbij, seven kinds of grain, in their name.

It is quiet, crowded and deeply moving. Come with patience and respect.

🙏 Our 3-day Pashupatinath Darshan includes morning darshan, the evening Bagmati Aarti and Guhyeshwari — private to your family, with Satvik meals on request. We can plan it around Bala Chaturdashi if you wish to be there.

Who would you light a lamp for? 👇

Temples, a lake under the mountains, and a one-horned rhino — Nepal's three faces in one week. 🛕🏔️🦏

Our 7-day Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan trip: the old squares of Kathmandu, sunrise over the Annapurna range from Sarangkot, a boat on Phewa Lake, then Chitwan National Park — jeep safari, a canoe on the Rapti and a Tharu cultural evening. Easy pace, private to your family.

Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath — the four dhams of the Garhwal Himalaya, in one yatra. 🙏

Most Char Dham journeys begin in Delhi. Ours begins where many families feel a yatra should: with darshan of Lord Shiva at Pashupatinath in Kathmandu.

🛕 Day 2 — Pashupatinath darshan & puja
🌊 Day 4 — cross at Sunauli, evening Ganga Aarti at Haridwar
🏔️ Days 6–12 — the four dhams, one by one
🌿 Day 13 — down to Rishikesh

14 days, private to your family. Pure-vegetarian Satvik meals on request, and helicopter or doli options at Kedarnath and Yamunotri for elderly parents. Indian nationals need no visa for Nepal.

Fifteen days on foot, to the foot of the highest mountain on earth. 🏔️ This is the Everest Base Camp Trek.

Fly to Lukla, climb through Namche Bazaar and Tengboche, reach Everest Base Camp at 5,364 m — then Kala Patthar (5,545 m) at dawn, the finest view of Everest on the whole route. Two acclimatisation days are built in. Private to your group, with a licensed guide and porters.

Coming to Nepal this winter? Pack for two seasons in one day. 🧥☀️

Winter mornings and nights are cold, while the afternoons are often bright and sunny. A few things make the trip far more comfortable:

🧣 Layers you can take off and put back on
🧥 A warm jacket and hat for sunrise viewpoints and evenings
🕶️ Sunscreen and sunglasses — the sun is strong, even when the air is cold
👟 Shoes you can slip off easily — you remove them at many temples, so bring warm socks
🔦 A small torch — the days are shorter
